nodes.name: Grant_Rubisco_C3_Kinetics

In a C4 PFT the same kinetics run in the bundle sheath on bundle-sheath CO2.

nodes.name: Turgor_Based_Stomatal_Stress
nodes.description: Stomatal resistance is the CO2-gradient-over-carboxylation resistance at a prescribed Ci:Ca (FCO2), bounded by a minimum and by the cuticular resistance (RSMX), and moved toward the cuticular value by EXP(-canopy turgor/RCS); turgor comes from canopy water potential and an osmotic potential set by OSMO and nonstructural solutes. The same stress sets photosynthesis (RSL, non-stomatal factor) and the transpiration resistance.

nodes.name: Canopy_Radiative_Transfer
nodes.description: Multilayer, multi-inclination, multi-azimuth canopy radiation: leaf SW and PAR albedo and transmittance (snow blended), a live-leaf clumping factor that starts at CFI and declines with leaf area and canopy snow, CLASS inclination fractions and leaf geometry place leaf area in sectors; a top-down sweep sets the sunlit fraction of each layer, and sunlit leaves absorb direct plus diffuse PAR while shaded leaves absorb diffuse only.

nodes.name: Node_Leaf_Phenology
nodes.description: Per-branch development. Node initiation (XRNI) and leaf appearance (XRLA) run at 25 oC rates times a leaf-growth Arrhenius factor of canopy temperature shifted by the ZTYPI offset (annuals also by water and O2 stress); normalised node counts advance an 11-stage calendar against the maturity group GROUPX-XTLI, with photoperiod (XDL, XPPD) at floral initiation; leaf-out and leaf-off hour accumulators (VRNLI, VRNXI) follow evergreen, cold-deciduous (CTC chilling penalty), drought-deciduous or cold+drought rules; new branches need turgor and canopy nonstructural C above PB. The leaf-out/leaf-off status gates photosynthesis, node growth, remobilization, storage mobilisation and perennial branch resets.

nodes.name: Stage_Prescribed_Allocation
nodes.description: Hard-coded, stage-dependent partition fractions of the C that branch growth consumes among leaf, petiole, stalk, stalk reserve, husk, ear and grain, converted to structure by per-organ growth yields (DM*); the yields also set the growth-respiration quotient, and growth is limited by nonstructural N and P priced at the organ stoichiometries.

nodes.name: MichaelisMenten_Nutrient_Uptake
nodes.description: Root and mycorrhizal uptake of NH4, NO3, H2PO4 and HPO4 per layer and band zone: capacity = Vmax x root surface area per plant x transporter density x root growth temperature function x C and N/P feedback, solved jointly with mass flow and diffusion to the root through a quadratic, capped by the solute mass above Cmin allotted by the previous hour's demand share.

nodes.name: Symbiotic_N2_Fixation
nodes.description: Root nodules (INTYP root types) and canopy nodules (INTYP canopy types) fix N2 from nodule growth respiration: fixation respiration = RGNDL*RGN2P/(RGNDL + RGN2P), fixation = that x EN2F (0.20 gN per gC), where RGN2P is the respiration needed to bring nodule N:C up to CNND.

nodes.name: Prescribed_Tissue_Stoichiometry
nodes.description: Prescribed organ N:C and P:C used to price and build new growth: leaf and sheath ratios after emergence (root ratios before), stalk, reserve (also for the grain partition), husk and ear exactly; leaf ratios are maxima scaled by nonstructural N,P status.

nodes.name: Root_Hydraulic_Architecture
nodes.description: Root radii and porosity set root length, surface and volume per unit C; radial (RSRR), fine-root axial (ARSRA, RVSR, RRAD2M), primary axial (ARSRA, RVSR) and stalk axial (RSSA) resistances in series with a soil resistance give each rooted layer's conductance for water uptake; layers act in parallel.

nodes.name: Leaf_Protein_Colimitation
nodes.description: Leaf protein, which carries the photosynthetic enzymes and chlorophyll, accumulates at the LESSER of an N route and a P route: the N content of new leaf growth times CNWL and its P content times CPWL. The N and P contents are set by CNLF and CPLF times (0.33 + 0.67*CNPG), CNPG being the branch nonstructural N,P saturation. Protein per leaf area sets Rubisco surface density and Vcmax.

nodes.name: Root_Growth_Allocation
nodes.description: Per layer and structural axis, root nonstructural C is oxidised at VMXCSpec (temperature, root water potential, root N/P status, grain-fill downregulation), maintenance is paid on structural N, the remainder drives growth limited by nonstructural N and P through FNP; growth yield DMRT converts consumed C to structure; RTFQ sets new fine-root axes; PR gates new structural axes.

nodes.name: Plant_Functional_Type_Switches
nodes.description: Integer PFT switches that select whole pathways (C3/C4, growth habit, development pattern, phenology type, photoperiod type, turnover, storage organ, growth type, embryophyte type, secondary growth).

nodes.name: Heterotroph_Aerobic_Catabolism
nodes.description: Monod DOC/acetate oxidation by aerobic heterotrophs, facultative denitrifiers (aerobic mode), aerobic N2 fixers and fungi, O2-limited; the same specific rate sets the activity proxy that drives hydrolysis; the CO2 is aggregated into the layer's net microbial CO2 exchange.

nodes.name: Microbial_Maintenance_Respiration
nodes.description: Maintenance demand proportional to biomass N, temperature and acidity; it partitions gross respiration between maintenance and growth and adds CO2 only when it exceeds supply (starvation).

nodes.name: Microbial_Mortality_Recycling
nodes.description: Live microbial biomass dies at a basal rate scaled by water/temperature and biomass density; a recycling fraction returns to the reserve (more for N and P than for C) and the rest goes to microbial residue or humus.

nodes.name: Growth_Efficiency_Energetics
nodes.description: Free-energy yields and growth energy costs set the fraction of substrate C respired per unit assimilated, used both as the substrate-limited respiration cap and to convert growth respiration into uptake.

nodes.name: SOM_Hydrolysis
nodes.description: Hydrolysis of the colonized fraction of solid SOM (litter, POM, humus) to DOM at a rate set by the microbial activity proxy per unit bulk C, a DOC-inhibited Monod on bulk SOC concentration and DOC product inhibition; litter complexes humify part of the product to POM.

nodes.name: Necromass_Hydrolysis
nodes.description: Hydrolysis of microbial residue (kinetic and recalcitrant) to DOM with the same activity-based scalar as SOM hydrolysis, capped twice.

nodes.name: DOM_Sorption_Desorption
nodes.description: Exchange of DOC, DON, DOP and acetate between solution and the sorbed pool toward a partition set by soil mass, anion exchange capacity and HSORP; sorbed OM returns to solution also by microbial hydrolysis.

nodes.name: Plant_Autotrophic_Respiration
nodes.description: Per branch, nonstructural C is oxidised at VMXC times the canopy growth temperature function, N/P status, grain fill and water status; maintenance RmSpecPlant*TFN5*structural N is paid first; the surplus, scaled by turgor, is growth respiration limited by nonstructural N and P through the growth-respiration quotient; the deficit triggers remobilization. Pre-emergence branches, roots and nodules use layer temperature functions; all terms, plus C4 leakage and grazing, accumulate negative in Eco_AutoR_CumYr_col.

nodes.name: Leaf_Area_Expansion
nodes.description: Organ geometry from new mass: leaf area grows by EtiolationCoeff*SLA1*dMC**SLA2*turgor per unit leaf C, where dMC is the per-plant leaf C of the growing node; sheath and internode lengths follow the same form with SSL1/SSL2 and SNL1/SNL2. Growth is spread over the concurrently growing nodes.

nodes.name: Shoot_Root_Nonstructural_Exchange
nodes.description: Each live branch exchanges nonstructural C with each root layer down to MaxSoilLays4Root_pft in proportion to a mass-weighted concentration gradient times the conductance PTSHTR; N and P follow N:C and P:C gradients, with a transpiration-driven root-to-shoot enhancement; every flux is limited to 0.9999 of the donor.

nodes.name: Coarse_Root_Thickening_Stoichiometry
nodes.description: Woody vascular PFTs with lcoarseroot = .true. thicken primary roots from layer nonstructural C at the live coarse-root N:C and P:C, update radius from active-zone volume, and transfer active to lignified (dead) structure once the radius exceeds dmax, returning the N and P difference between live and dead ratios to the nonstructural pool; medium roots branch at MRTFQ and split growth between thickening and elongation by the cytokinin scalar CYTOS.

nodes.name: Microbial_N_P_Mineralization_Immobilization
nodes.description: Each heterotroph guild compares its reserve N (P) with reserve C times the target reserve N:C (P:C). Below target it immobilizes NH4 then NO3 (H2PO4 then HPO4) by Michaelis-Menten kinetics within its competitive share of the pool; at or above target it releases the excess as NH4 (H2PO4). The layer totals become the microbial source or sink of the soil mineral solution pools.

nodes.name: Soil_Mineral_N_P_Supply_To_Roots
nodes.description: Roots take NH4, NO3 and H2PO4 from the same soil solution pools the microbes exchange with, each uptaker limited to its share of the previous hour's total root plus microbial demand; uptake leaves the soil as a solute sink and enters root nonstructural N and P.

nodes.name: Plant_Nonstructural_N_P_To_Leaf_Protein
nodes.description: Root nonstructural N and P move to the branches down the nonstructural concentration gradient; branch nonstructural N and P status sets the N:C and P:C of new leaf growth; new leaf N and P build leaf protein, and leaf protein sets Rubisco (and PEP carboxylase for C4) and so Vcmax.

nodes.name: Microbial_Reserve_To_Structural_Growth
nodes.description: Each guild moves reserve C to its kinetic and structural compartments at an hourly rate scaled by temperature and water, carrying reserve N and P in proportion; kinetic C sets the active biomass that drives every catabolic and hydrolysis rate.

nodes.name: Heterotroph_Fermentation_Catabolism
nodes.description: Fermenters and anaerobic N2 fixers oxidize DOC under O2 inhibition; two thirds of the respired C becomes acetate and one third CO2, with H2 as a by-product.

nodes.name: Evapotranspiration_Accumulation
nodes.description: ECO_ET_col is the year-to-date sum of hourly ground plus canopy vapour loss, m2mm*QEvap_CumYr_col/AREA, with QEvap_CumYr_col -= VapXAir2GSurf_col + QVegET_col each hour and a reset on day 1; the ground term sums bare-soil, snow and litter vapour exchange over the NPH iterations, the canopy term sums transpiration plus interception evaporation and sublimation over active PFTs.

nodes.name: Canopy_Transpiration
nodes.description: Per-PFT transpiration Transpiration_pft = EX*Rb/(Rb+Rs), EX = CdVapCanopyAir*(VPA - VPLeaf) less any interception evaporation already taken, VPLeaf from the Kelvin relation on canopy water potential; Rs from CalcStomataResist4H2O = Rmin + (Rcut - Rmin)*exp(-turgor/RCS); solved jointly with canopy temperature and the root-uptake water balance.

nodes.name: Canopy_Interception_Evaporation
nodes.description: Rain and snow are intercepted up to capacities FoliarWatRetcap(IGTYP class) and FoliarSnowRetcap(ISNTYP class) times leaf+stalk area, snow is unloaded by wind and above 270 K; held water evaporates at EX*Rb/(Rb+ResistLeafSurf), first liquid then sublimation of held snow, and condensation goes to the canopy surface as dew.

nodes.name: Ground_Evaporation_And_Condensation
nodes.description: Bare-soil vapour flux VapXAir2TopLay = max(CdSoiEvap*(VPQ_col - VaporSoi1), -TopLayWatVol*dts_wat) with the Kelvin soil vapour pressure on matric plus osmotic potential; litter evaporation CdLitREvap*(VPQ_col - VapLitR); snow evaporation then sublimation CdSnoEvap*(VPQ_col - vapsat(Tsnow)); all exchange with canopy air VPQ_col built from last hour's total latent flux.

nodes.name: Litter_Layer_Vapour_Resistance
nodes.description: Litter adds a diffusive resistance DLYRR/(TEFGASDIF(T)*7.70E-2) divided by the litter tortuosity thetaA^2*POROQ/POROS; the ground boundary-layer resistance is the litter-fraction-weighted harmonic mean of the open and litter-covered paths, Richardson-clamped, and it sets both bare-soil evaporation and the soil-atmosphere gas conductance.

nodes.name: Ground_Radiation_Balance
nodes.description: Ground net radiation Radnet2Grnd = (1 - AlbedoGrnd)*SW + LW_in - emissivity*sigma*T^4, with AlbedoGrnd the mass-weighted mix of the grid soil albedo ALBS, water 0.06 and ice 0.30 in the top layer; the canopy radiation model instead reflects ground radiation with a moisture-independent albedo equal to ALBS.

nodes.name: Below_Canopy_Aerodynamic_Resistance
nodes.description: Ground aerodynamic resistance from the Choudhury-Monteith (1988) within-canopy profile using a hard-coded ground roughness (0.020 m on soil, ZW = 0.01 m on water or snow), plus the above-canopy log-profile resistance whose roughness length is floored by the same ground roughness.

nodes.name: Soil_Gas_Ebullition
nodes.description: Aqueous gas above the amount the layer water can hold at atmospheric plus ponding pressure is removed by half the excess per iteration, sweeping upward from NLF_col, and emitted when the layer is the surface or below the water table, otherwise moved to that layer's gas phase.

nodes.name: Harvest_Cutting_Partition
nodes.description: Management harvest and cutting. On a management day, at solar noon (grazing and herbivory hourly), each organ group loses the fraction above the cut height times its PFT-level harvest fraction (ECUT11-14), or the population fraction THIN (PCUT); population is scaled by (1 - THIN). Of the removed mass the ecosystem-level fraction (ECUT21-24) is exported (plant disturbance loss, harvest accumulator, NBP debit) and the rest goes to surface litter, or for woody plants partly back to standing dead. Standing dead then decays to surface litter at a fixed hourly rate scaled by the canopy-growth temperature function.

nodes.name: Plant_Death_Root_Litterfall_And_Replanting
nodes.description: What happens to a plant's root mass when the plant dies, is disturbed, or is replanted. When the roots die, ResetDeadPlant calls SetDeadPlant, LiterFallDeadRoots and LiterFallRootShootStorage, which move the root pools to litter layer by layer, and ResetBranchRootStates then zeroes the root states. Tillage, harvest thinning, annual death and annual termination remove root mass layer by layer too. On a planting day a plant slot that is not active is re-initialised by StartPlants, and InitRootMychorMorphoBio zeroes every root pool over all layers 1..NL. Every one of those removal loops ends at MaxNumRootLays, one layer short of NK = MaxNumRootLays + 1, the deepest layer roots grow into.

nodes.name: Soil_Water_Retention_Derivation
nodes.description: Each soil layer's field capacity FC, wilting point WP and vertical and lateral saturated conductivities SCNV, SCNH come from the grid file only when the file value is non-negative. A negative value is a sentinel: ComputeSoilHydroPars marks the property isoi_unset for that layer and, for a sentinel FC (WP), resets the column potential PSIFC (PSIWP) to -0.033 (-1.5) MPa. On a cold start SoilHydroProperty keeps the file FC and WP only when BOTH are set; if either is unset SetColdRunSoilStates recomputes BOTH from texture, organic C, bulk density and macropore fraction: mineral soil (organic C < FORGW) FC = 0.2576 - 0.20*sand + 0.36*clay + 0.60E-6*C and WP = 0.0260 + 0.50*clay + 0.32E-6*C; organic soil by bulk-density class (FC 0.27/0.62/0.71, WP 0.04/0.15/0.22); then FC/(1-macropore fraction) capped at 0.75*porosity and WP/(1-macropore fraction) capped at 0.75*FC. A sentinel SCNV or SCNH is derived from porosity and the field-capacity water content (mineral) or from bulk density (organic). On a restart the stored FC and WP are used unchanged. LOGPSIFLD = log(-PSIFC) and LOGPSIMN = log(-PSIWP) anchor the retention curve that converts water content to matric potential.
